subject: Planned tenant-affinity rotation + staged warm restarts in East US 3 (Nov 9)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme.com, infra@brighthealth.ai
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 14:00:00 -0800
Subject: Planned tenant-affinity rotation + staged warm restarts in East US 3 (Nov 9)

Hi everyone,

Quick note to let you know we have a planned maintenance window for the East US 3 region on Mon, Nov 9, 00:30–03:30 UTC (run broken into small staged batches). This work is a tenant-affinity rotation combined with staged warm restarts to harmonize a driver ABI across the fleet.

Why we're doing this
- Upstream kernel/driver ABI divergence has started to affect tail latency on a small subset of long-lived sessions.
- The rotation + warm restarts let us converge kernel/driver combinations while preserving KV cache where possible.

Expected impact
- Most customers: no API downtime. You may see transient latency spikes (sub-2s) for in-flight requests during the brief handoff.
- A small fraction of long-lived sessions may experience cache eviction if they are pinned to hosts that are rotated; we expect less than 0.5% of tokens served in this window to be regenerated.
- We will not evict running jobs intentionally; customers that run large batch jobs should expect potential delay in scheduling until their tenancy is restored.

Operational details
- Start: 2026-11-09T00:30:00Z; End: 2026-11-09T03:30:00Z (approx).
- Work happens in micro-batches per host pool; we will avoid broad pool-wide drains.
- Prefix/KV cache preservation is enabled; where preservation is impossible we will fall back to a short-lived cache flush and warm KV refill.
- If you need to opt out for a specific project or dataset, fill the opt-out form (link below) by 2026-11-08 22:00 UTC. Opt-outs will be honored where capacity allows.

Attachments: maintenance_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook), kv-preservation-checklist.xlsx (customer-facing checklist)
Links: https://support.redwood.com/maintenance-opt-out-form?id=EUS3-11-09

If you have hard latency SLOs for November 9 that would be impacted by any drift, please reply with the project name and sample endpoints so we can prioritize affinity exclusions.

Thanks,
—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Program Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Linda Park <ops@acme.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Planned tenant-affinity rotation + staged warm restarts in East US 3 (Nov 9)

Thanks for the heads up, Stephanie. Two quick questions from our side:

1) Our production chat service keeps a hot KV cache for short-term context (session TTL ~30m). If an eviction happens and KV refill occurs, what typical time to steady-state do you see for session-level cache rehydration?
2) Is there a way to request an exclusion for a single pool (project: acme-chat-prod) rather than full opt-out? We still want the maintenance broadly, just avoid the chat pool.

If you can provide an estimated burst risk (percentage of requests that might see >1s extra latency) that would help our on-call.

—Linda
Linda Park
SRE, ACME Solutions

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme.com, infra@brighthealth.ai
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Planned tenant-affinity rotation + staged warm restarts in East US 3 (Nov 9)

Hi Linda — good questions. Technical notes below and a short checklist attached.

TL;DR
- Expected KV rehydration to steady-state: 3–7 minutes for an average session (dependent on traffic pattern and prefix cache hit rate).
- We can apply an affinity exclusion at the project/pool level. To request this, reply with the Redwood project ID or the pool name; we need 4 hours lead time to lock the exclusion.
- Expected extra-latency burst for affected requests: ~0.2–1.5s for the brief handoff window; worst-case tail rarer than 0.05% of requests.

More detail
- Preservation behavior: We attempt prefix-level KV merge before fallback to flush. When merge succeeds, clients see no re-evaluation. When merge is impossible (driver-state mismatch), we stream a quick refill; refill time depends on token-generation rate for that session.
- Exclusion process: we mark tenancy in the routing layer to avoid selecting hosts scheduled for rotation. This is per-project and can be scoped to a pool tag (e.g., project:acme-chat-prod).

Action items for ACME
1) Reply with the project ID or pool name if you want exclusion.
2) If you opt into exclusion, note that we may use spare capacity in neighboring pools for failover; network egress patterns could change briefly.

Attachments: kv-preservation-checklist.xlsx (step-by-step client checklist for minimizing refill impact)

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Linda Park <ops@acme.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 18:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Planned tenant-affinity rotation + staged warm restarts in East US 3 (Nov 9)

Appreciate the details, Grace. Please apply an exclusion for project acme-chat-prod (ID: acme-prod-0912). We'll accept potential egress pattern changes. No other projects need exclusion.

—Linda
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme.com
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:20:00 -0800
Subject: Post-maintenance: East US 3 rotation — outcome and quick recap

Hi Linda / ACME team — quick post-maintenance update.

Summary
- Window: 2026-11-09T00:30Z–2026-11-09T03:10Z (completed early).
- Your exclusion (acme-prod-0912) was applied and verified; no cache evictions were observed for the excluded pool.
- End-to-end observed impact for non-excluded tenants: short transient latency spikes during host handoff (median +0.18s; 99.9th percentile +1.9s).
- We encountered one host that required a full restart (rather than a warm restart) due to a driver handshake failure; that host was drained and restored within a single micro-batch and the automated rollback prevented broader disruption. No customer-visible errors were reported.

Next steps
- We will publish a short postmortem (INF-8732) with timeline and mitigation details by Tue, Nov 11.
- If you want a live readout or raw traces for your project, reply and we'll schedule a 30-min runbook review.

Thanks for the coordination and for providing the project ID promptly — that made exclusion quick.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Manager, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference
